title: Bookmarks page requests /api/saves in an endless loop for users with no bookmarks
steps: Sign in locally as a user with no saved items and open /bookmarks.
Count requests for 10 s (scratch probe; same logic as scripts/browser/a11y-scan.cjs timing out on /bookmarks).
expected: One GET /api/saves when the page opens.
actual: 1,777 GET /api/saves in 10 s (≈178/s) and never stops. The effect re-runs whenever savedIds changes; hydrate() stores a new empty object when the user has no saves, which changes savedIds and re-triggers the effect.
impact: In production the global limit (500 requests / 15 min per IP) is reached in about 3 s, after which every API call from that person — and anyone sharing their IP (mobile carrier NAT, office) — fails with 429 for 15 minutes. It also burns server CPU and the Upstash Redis daily quota (TD-023). Most new users have no bookmarks.
fix: Add an `hydrated` flag to the bookmarks store and run the effect once (`useEffect(() => { if (!hydrated) hydrate(); }, [hydrated, hydrate])`), or move the list to TanStack Query. Add a Vitest test that renders Bookmarks with an empty response and asserts one request.
regression_test: Vitest: Bookmarks with empty /api/saves issues exactly one request; Playwright: request count on /bookmarks stays < 5 over 5 s.
